## Diagnosis

The error path in `parse_binding` (parser.py:169-176) recovers with `_rest_of_line = r"[^
]*(?:|
|
)?"`. On CRLF input, the alternation `|
|
` matches `` first, leaving the `
` unconsumed. So the invalid binding's `original.string` ends at ``, and the next `parse_binding` starts at the stray `
` — producing a spurious empty binding and shifting the valid binding's line/string. LF and lone CR work because a single char is consumed.

## Change plan

Reorder the alternation to `(?:
||
)?` so CRLF is consumed as one unit (mirroring `_newline`/`_end_of_line`). This makes the invalid binding's `original.string` include the full CRLF, keeps the valid binding starting at line 2 with `original.string == "GOOD=ok
"`, and preserves LF/CR and repeated invalid lines. Optionally add a CRLF recovery test to `tests/test_parser.py`. No other files need changes.
